findings.reason: a literal implementation leaves the roadmap on a different age source from the audit, so either §3 must state that the first call gains a path or it must drop the "one age" claim for the roadmap.
findings.text: §3 says "every caller of `derived_plan_age` passes the new arguments: both calls in the roadmap's `_authorisation_age` (the first passes no path today, the second a fallback path)" and that the three consumers "report one age", yet the commit lookup it adds is keyed by "look[ing] the plan up in that map" — which needs the plan path — and `reckon/roadmap.py:945` supplies none (`plan.get("modified") or plan.get("last")` with `created_at=plan.get("created")`, so the first call returns `plan-modified` or `file-created` non-None and `reckon/roadmap.py:968`'s path-bearing call is reached only when both are absent); the roadmap therefore cannot report the commit age the audit reports

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §3 cites functions and modules by name; `derived_plan_age` (`reckon/doccheck.py:239`), `_git_last_committed(repo_dir, docs_dir)` (`reckon/serve.py:1532`), `_commit_days` (`reckon/fleet_index.py:45`), `reckon/archive.py:87`, `reckon/roadmap.py:945/968`, and the three direct callers in `tests/test_doccheck.py` (lines 124/135/150) all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3 names a measurable outcome (an `AGING` row with age 20 and source `commit`, a 40-day plan reported `STALE`) and an executed negative control (age read from the mtime → age 0, no row, test fails).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the write paths are repository sources and test files under `tests/`; no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file is named by what it measures (`tests/test_staleness_counts_from_the_last_commit.py`), and `AGING`/`STALE` are emitted audit codes, not plan or ticket labels.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 claims every caller passes the new arguments and that the audit, the roadmap and the archive then report one age, but the roadmap's first `derived_plan_age` call passes no plan path, so the commit-first read cannot apply there and the roadmap's age stays the plan-modified/file-created figure the audit no longer reports.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 carries one deliverable: one age owner, one new audit code (`AGING`), one migration of its callers.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3 declares its order after §2 in prose ("This section runs after §2, which also writes `doccheck.py`") and in followup f-tprt-002, and gate `g-tprt-age-honest` names `the-portfolio-reads-true#s3`.
